report.title: Core computational systems for LLM-assisted qualitative coding and thematic analysis
notes: Publication status was verified against official publisher/repository records where possible.
LLM-TA, Auto-TA, SFT-TA, TAMA, and Yi et al. 2026 provenance reuse the same nine AAOCA focus-group transcripts and 12 human reference themes; they are not independent dataset replications.
Claimed methodology and operationalized task are stored separately.

studies.citation: Dai, Shih-Chieh; Xiong, Aiping; Ku, Lun-Wei. 2023. LLM-in-the-loop: Leveraging Large Language Model for Thematic Analysis. Findings of EMNLP 2023, 9993–10001.
studies.operationalized_method: iterative human–LLM codebook construction followed by deductive code assignment; codebook/coding-reliability TA
studies.architecture: single LLM interacting iteratively with a human; no agents
studies.prompting: 4–8 few-shot exemplars; temperature 0; full prompts Appendix D
studies.human_role: human coder supplies examples, edits/rationalizes and stops; independent third coder evaluates
datasets: Music Shuffle: 397 participants/four questions; 35 answers analyzed
Password Manager: 277 participants/eight questions; 280 answers to selected question; 100 development plus 20 seen and 20 unseen evaluation
studies.results: Human–machine kappa .87/.81; original-gold .66/.77; third-coder–machine .54/.47; Password seen/unseen .80/.82; cosine .8864/.8895; accuracy .84/.83; recall .72/.87.
studies.ethics: public non-sensitive data; API disclosure/IRB and pretraining-contamination risks discussed
studies.reproducibility: code https://github.com/sjdai/LLM-thematic-analysis; prompts public; proprietary unsnapshotted model
studies.limitations: small evaluation subsets; consensus-gold assumption; possible pretraining exposure

studies.citation: Parfenova, Angelina; Denzler, Alexander; Pfeffer, Juergen. 2024. Automating Qualitative Data Analysis with Large Language Models. ACL Student Research Workshop, 83–91.
studies.status: peer-reviewed PhD proposal; no completed system evaluation
studies.operationalized_method: proposed sentence-summary open codes and contextual LLM grouping; not empirically operationalized
models: several LoRA-fine-tuned LLMs proposed; exact models not reported
studies.prompting: zero-/few-shot proposed; exact prompts not reported
studies.human_role: experts proposed to curate labels and evaluate output
datasets: curated interview quote–label data proposed; size not reported
studies.ethics: anonymization, consent, regulation, bias/fairness/transparency, labor displacement and environmental cost discussed

studies.citation: Parfenova, Angelina; Marfurt, Andreas; Denzler, Alexander; Pfeffer, Juergen. 2025. Text Annotation via Inductive Coding: Comparing Human Experts to LLMs in Qualitative Data Analysis. Findings of NAACL 2025, 6471–6484.
studies.operationalized_method: supervised generation of one short code per presegmented quote/sentence; no axial/theme construction evaluation
studies.architecture: single causal LM with zero/few-shot or LoRA
studies.model_versions: Hugging Face IDs reported; commit hashes not reported
studies.prompting: zero-shot and 1/3/5-shot; six prompt variants; LoRA r16/alpha32/dropout .05; max_new_tokens 15, temperature .7, top_p .7
studies.human_role: three researchers code and rate 15 selected sentences
datasets: 600 social-science quote–code pairs across nine sources
studies.results: Best BERTScore F1 about .766; TinyLlama five-shot .755; human alpha .20; LLMs better on selected easy items, humans on difficult items.
studies.reproducibility: prompts/settings described; code/data release not reported
studies.limitations: no validation set; 15-item human study; low agreement undermines gold labels

studies.citation: Parfenova, Angelina; Pfeffer, Jürgen. 2025. Measuring What Matters: Evaluating Ensemble LLMs with Label Refinement in Inductive Coding. Findings of ACL 2025, 10803–10816.
studies.claimed_method: ensemble inductive coding and label refinement
studies.operationalized_method: candidate labels from three models, moderator selection/new label, sequential embedding reuse
studies.architecture: multiple candidate LMs plus moderator; sequential refinement memory
studies.prompting: LoRA and generation settings largely follow Parfenova 2025; exact full configuration in appendices
studies.human_role: manual reference codes; tiny 10-item score-correlation validation; number of experts not reported
metrics: equal composite of normalized cosine, METEOR, code-length penalty and JSD
studies.results: Refined Mixtral .99 at threshold .7 vs .33 standalone; Llama-70B .74 vs .38; GPT-4 refinement .54 vs .74; human-score Spearman .73, p=.039 on 10 items.
studies.ethics: anonymization, bias and human oversight discussed
studies.limitations: gold-dependent post-hoc metric; threshold selection unclear; no validation split; tiny human validation

studies.citation: Zhong, Mian; Wang, Pristina; Field, Anjalie. 2025. HICode: Hierarchical Inductive Coding with LLMs. EMNLP 2025, 31060–31078.
studies.claimed_method: hierarchical inductive coding inspired by qualitative research
studies.operationalized_method: targeted automated schema induction: per-segment short labels then repeated batched LLM clustering/synthesis
studies.architecture: two-stage pipeline with iterative clustering; no human in evaluated loop
models: Mixtral Large exact version not reported
studies.prompting: goal/background conditioned; labels <=5 words; full prompts Appendix A; temperatures not reported
studies.chunking: paragraph segments; random batches of 100 labels
studies.human_role: supplies goal/background; may browse hierarchy; no intervention in evaluation pipeline
studies.results: At threshold .4 HICode P/R: Values .96/.57, Astro .53/.51, Frame .68/.81; human Astro .72/.74; TopicGPT .18/.33; Astro human alpha .31.
studies.ethics: not reported as a dedicated participant-data ethics issue for public/benchmark sources
studies.reproducibility: code https://github.com/mianzg/HICode; prompts available; embedding model and some exact model versions not reported
studies.limitations: embedding metric validity, plural valid schemas, limited domains/models, prompt dependence

studies.citation: Rao, Varun Nagaraj; Agarwal, Eesha; Dalal, Samantha; Calacci, Dana; Monroy-Hernández, Andrés. 2025. QuaLLM: An LLM-based Framework to Extract Quantitative Insights from Online Forums. Findings of NAACL 2025, 1355–1369.
studies.claimed_method: qualitative concern extraction supporting quantitative insight
studies.operationalized_method: positivist four-stage concern generation, classification, aggregation/ranking and prevalence estimation
studies.architecture: single-model multi-prompt pipeline plus BERTopic aggregation analysis
studies.prompting: five submissions/comments per call; seven-step JSON prompt; no-outside-knowledge instruction; temperature/seeds not reported
studies.chunking: groups of five Reddit submissions plus comments
studies.human_role: defines 4–5 categories, builds small references, selects representative quotes
studies.results: Factuality .55, completeness .78; classification/prevalence accuracy .74/.82; BERTopic distinctness .80 and coverage@1 .95/@2 1.00; cost $1,662.30 and 145.49M total tokens.
studies.ethics: public-forum privacy/consent trade-offs, profanity/API selection bias, misinformation and model bias discussed
studies.reproducibility: prompt details and topic hyperparameters reported; code/data resource not reported; proprietary snapshot missing
studies.limitations: small audits, 11% failures, reporting discrepancy about annotators, positivist reduction, stochasticity

studies.citation: Qiao, Tingrui; Walker, Caroline; Cunningham, Chris; Koh, Yun Sing. 2025. Thematic-LM: A Multi-Agent Large Language Model Framework for Enhancing Automated Thematic Analysis. The Web Conference 2025, 649–658.
studies.operationalized_method: autonomous code/theme generation, aggregation and reviewer-managed adaptive codebook
studies.architecture: AutoGen; coder, aggregator and reviewer agents; SentenceTransformer retrieval; LLMLingua compression
studies.prompting: JSON mode; default temperature 1/top_p 1; 2 coding coders and 2 theme coders; identity prompts
studies.chunking: not reported; codebook retains max 20 quotes/code/theme and retrieves top 10 similar entries
studies.human_role: no independent analyst in main pipeline
datasets: Dreaddit source >190,000 posts; exact processed count not reported
climate Reddit source >4.6M posts/comments; exact processed count not reported
studies.results: Dreaddit C/D/T: single .63/.45/.41; system2 .94/.78/.87. Climate: single .66/.56/.73; system2 .98/.86/.89.
studies.reproducibility: code not located; proprietary unsnapshotted model; three runs but seeds not reported
studies.limitations: same-family self-evaluation; ROUGE mapped weakly to trustworthiness; no independent human evaluation; identity prompts may stereotype

studies.citation: Lam, Michelle S.; Teoh, Janice; Landay, James A.; Heer, Jeffrey; Bernstein, Michael S. 2024. Concept Induction: Analyzing Unstructured Text with High-Level Concepts Using LLooM. CHI 2024.
studies.operationalized_method: mixed-initiative filter/summarize, embedding cluster, concept synthesize, score and loop workflow; not formal TA
studies.architecture: LLM operators plus HDBSCAN/embeddings and interactive workbench; no agents
studies.prompting: temperature 0; full prompts Appendix A; max 200 induction items and 20 concepts
studies.chunking: item/document level; batch details in paper
studies.human_role: analyst inspects, edits, adds, merges, splits and rescores; two expert case studies
studies.results: Bills coverage .74 vs GPT-4-Turbo .56; Wikipedia .81 vs GPT-4 .83; mean classification accuracy .91/precision .70/recall .59/F1 .59; human-human kappa .64, LLooM-human .63/.645.
studies.ethics: analyst anchoring/bias and proprietary-model concerns discussed
studies.reproducibility: code https://github.com/michelle123lam/lloom; prompts public; model snapshots missing
studies.limitations: untested defaults, stochastic/domain variability, hallucination, cost, proprietary drift, only two one-hour expert sessions

studies.citation: Sharma, Ansh; Wallace, James R. 2025. DeTAILS: Deep Thematic Analysis with Iterative LLM Support. CUI 2025, 1–7. Expanded preprint: Sharma, Cochrane, Wallace, arXiv:2510.17575v2.
studies.status: peer-reviewed short CUI paper plus distinct expanded non-peer-reviewed preprint
studies.operationalized_method: interactive RAG-assisted editable codebook, global coding, code clustering/review and theme buckets; hybrid/codebook TA
studies.architecture: Electron/React, Python, ChromaDB RAG, Ollama, LangChain adapters
studies.model_versions: Gemini preview identifier reported; other models user-configurable
studies.prompting: chain-of-thought mentioned; exact prompts/hyperparameters not reported
studies.chunking: 30 Reddit threads per participant initially; implementation chunk sizes not reported
studies.human_role: researcher can revise, accept, revisit and backtrack at every stage
datasets: expanded preprint: 18 researchers, six per expertise level
30 Reddit threads each plus precomputed December 2024 month corpus
studies.results: F1 .86 related concepts, .98 outline, .90 initial coding, .97 global, .90 review codes, 1.00 themes; NASA-TLX 26.3/100; usefulness 4.21/5.
studies.reproducibility: code https://github.com/DaemonOnCode/DeTAILS; expanded preprint has template errors; prompts absent
studies.limitations: alignment is not truth and may reflect anchoring; no comparator; Reddit only; short sessions; one evaluated model

studies.citation: Chen, John et al. 2026. A Computational Method for Measuring ‘Open Codes’ in Qualitative Analysis. Findings of ACL 2026, 41740–41758.
studies.operationalized_method: aggregate code-space construction through embedding/LLM merge, then Coverage/Overlap/Novelty/Divergence diagnostics
studies.architecture: four-stage merge/evaluation pipeline; not a code generator
studies.prompting: four machine coders use varied prompts; Gemma temperature .5; full prompts in paper/package claim
studies.human_role: four human coders create parallel codebooks
datasets: 127 anonymized public Physics Lab community messages
studies.results: CoV <.1 and adjusted R2 >.91 generally; flooding increases coverage to 78.7 and divergence 67.3; hallucination reduces coverage to 35.6 and raises divergence 75.7; combined 1,775 vs 514 codes.
studies.ethics: IRB/anonymization; local-model preference; cloud/privacy, metric reification and automation-bias warnings
studies.reproducibility: CC BY-NC 4.0 package/data claimed, but repository URL not visible in inspected text
studies.limitations: team-relative shared omissions; flooding can be rewarded; no universal threshold; one domain and simulated extremes

studies.citation: Wang, Lei; Huang, Min; Dragut, Eduard. 2026. CentaurTA: A Self-Improving Human-Agents Collaboration Framework for Thematic Analysis. Findings of ACL 2026, 15871–15884.
studies.operationalized_method: Actor/Critic open coding and theme generation; human feedback distilled to persistent prompt principles, no weight updates
studies.architecture: sequential Actor/Critic agents plus prompt optimizer and simulated-expert drafts
studies.prompting: feedback updates prompts; temperature/seeds/token limits not reported
studies.human_role: six paid participants provide iterative feedback and rubric judgments; domain experts finalize simulated labels
studies.results: >90% batch accuracy after ~20 feedback items; on 300 USRS codes LLM-judge accuracy 90 vs human 89, kappa .68; full 90%/25 min vs human-only 90%/42 min.
studies.ethics: first two datasets IRB/anonymized; participants paid $20/hour
studies.limitations: small human sample; open models not tested; rubric incomplete; scores decline after ~10 iterations

studies.citation: Yi, Seungjun et al. 2025. Auto-TA: Towards Scalable Automated Thematic Analysis via Multi-Agent Large Language Models with Reinforcement Learning. arXiv:2506.23998v2.
studies.status: arXiv preprint; peer-reviewed venue not verified
studies.claimed_method: fully automated reflexive/end-to-end TA with multi-agent LLMs and reinforcement learning
studies.operationalized_method: sequential role-prompted coding, theme generation and critic edits; RLHF/PPO not implemented in results
studies.architecture: four coder identities, theme roles and critic; no agent-to-agent dialogue
studies.prompting: temperature 0; role prompts; full prompt details incomplete
studies.human_role: none in main run; optional future RLHF
datasets: AAOCA: 9 focus groups/42 parents/mean 10,987 words; appendix inconsistently says 85 participants
studies.results: Baseline C/D/T .8213/.400/.308; best role credibility .9841; theme-reference cosine baseline .132 vs roles .107–.121.
studies.reproducibility: no code/data availability statement found; contradictory iteration limits and role labels
studies.limitations: one corpus; no true RL; no agent interaction; construct-invalid metric labels; prompt sensitivity

studies.citation: Yi, Seungjun et al. 2025. SFT-TA: Supervised Fine-Tuned Agents in Multi-Agent LLMs for Automated Inductive Thematic Analysis. arXiv:2509.17167v1; ML4H 2025 manuscript.
studies.status: arXiv/ML4H manuscript; PDF has PMLR XXX placeholder; final archival status not verified
studies.claimed_method: automated inductive TA with supervised fine-tuned agents
studies.operationalized_method: sequential coder/aggregator/theme/refinement pipeline with two GPT-4o SFT roles and limited human filtering
studies.architecture: multi-role sequential pipeline; one SFT coding agent and one SFT theme-generation agent
studies.model_versions: exact snapshots and fine-tuning hyperparameters not reported
studies.prompting: chain-of-thought, structured tags, qualitative-researcher identity, exactly 12 themes, eight clinician criteria
studies.chunking: manually condensed transcripts; process not described/released
studies.human_role: removes off-topic output; four blinded raters; original experts supply reference themes
datasets: 10 reference themes paraphrased 30 times = 300 training points; 2 called validation
studies.results: Full SFT fuzzy .560, cosine .268, BLEU .080, METEOR .348, credibility .783, dependability .394, transferability .303; human coverage 5.00, actionability 4.28, distinctiveness 4.35, relevance 4.63.
studies.reproducibility: data/code unavailable, access by request; prompts/settings incomplete
studies.limitations: reference leakage because 10/12 evaluation themes shape SFT; one corpus; no inter-rater reliability; automatic/human metric mismatch

studies.citation: Xu, Huimin et al. 2026. TAMA: A Human-AI Collaborative Thematic Analysis Framework Using Multi-Agent LLMs for Clinical Interviews. ACM Transactions on Computing for Healthcare.
studies.operationalized_method: sequential role prompting for generation/evaluation/refinement with cardiac-expert review and stopping
studies.architecture: sequential roles, explicitly not contemporary interacting multi-agent architecture
studies.prompting: GPT-4o temperature 0; expert context/rubric; automatic threshold 4.5 abandoned for expert stopping
studies.human_role: cardiac expert sets context/rubric, reviews iterations and stops; expert also original coder
datasets: 12 themes from surgeon plus two qualitative coders; ~30 hours/person
studies.results: GPT-4o single .42/.83/.57; TAMA .29/.92/.55; human .33/1/.53. Llama single .20/.12/.34; TAMA .68/.08/.35. One-transcript judge: 0/13 hallucinations, grounding .95.
studies.ethics: de-identification; paper-specific IRB identifier not reported; API privacy risk discussed
studies.reproducibility: code https://github.com/Charlie-Yi-SJ/TAMA; dataset restricted; model snapshot missing
studies.limitations: one corpus; expert confirmation risk; same-family hallucination judge; metric naming ambiguity; fixed threshold over-refined

studies.citation: Yi, Seungjun et al. 2026. Automated Thematic Analysis for Clinical Qualitative Data: Iterative Codebook Refinement with Full Provenance. arXiv:2603.08989v1.
studies.status: arXiv preprint; peer-reviewed venue not verified
studies.claimed_method: automated TA with iterative codebook refinement and full provenance
studies.operationalized_method: quote-grounded code induction, LLM relation graph cleanup, Auto-TA theme construction, refinement and theme-to-turn ledger
studies.architecture: LOGOS-style graph codebook plus Auto-TA theme stages
studies.prompting: default 20 codes/chunk, labels 5–12 words, descriptions 40–80 words; evaluator temperature .3; other temperatures/full prompts not reported
studies.chunking: default 8,000 characters operationally; experiment 2,048 words with 200 overlap
studies.human_role: mostly automated; no independent human validation
studies.results: LOGOS best composite AAOCA .509, SVCHD .688, Ali .533, Dreaddit .462; Sheffield Thematic-LM .629 vs LOGOS .571; human cosine AAOCA .487/SVCHD .494.
studies.limitations: adaptive test leakage selecting Best on held-out test composite; same-model generator/judge; baseline reimplementations; no independent humans

models: GPT-family model; exact snapshot not reported in this extraction
studies.prompting: not reported in this extraction; repository should be pinned before reuse
studies.human_role: reference themes and clinical framing; prospective human workflow not evaluated
datasets: same 9 AAOCA focus groups/42 parents/12 reference themes
studies.results: see primary full text; detailed numerical extraction not completed in this track

studies.reproducibility: code https://github.com/jiaweixu98/LLM-TA; venue/status and model snapshot uncertain

studies.citation: Yi, Seungjun et al. 2025. Position: Thematic Analysis of Unstructured Clinical Transcripts with Large Language Models. arXiv:2509.14597v2.

studies.claimed_method: systematic review plus clinician interview and evaluation position
